title: UMass loses tight game to former conference foe NIU
dek: AMHERST, Mass. — There is a version of this game that UMass wins, and it is not hard to see. The Minutemen had the ball longer, ran more plays, committed fewer penalties and took the ball away one more time than they gave it up.
body:
**NIU 20, Massachusetts 14** · Week 2 · Sept. 12

AMHERST, Mass. — There is a version of this game that UMass wins, and it is not hard to see. The Minutemen had the ball longer, ran more plays, committed fewer penalties and took the ball away one more time than they gave it up. They erased a seven-point deficit and tied the game with 1:01 left in the first half.

Then NIU's Ryan Short kicked a 45-yard field goal with one second on the clock, and the tie was gone. UMass did not score again.

The result is a 20-14 loss in the home opener at Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium, and a 0-2 start for a team that needs six wins to reach a bowl. It is also the kind of loss that is hard to explain with a single number, and it was decided by a handful of moments rather than a collapse.

## How it unfolded

The first quarter ended 7-7, and it was a strange one. NIU scored first on a run from Eric Tafoya. UMass answered with a touchdown that came off a dropped punt, recovered by the Minutemen for the score. NIU then moved back in front when Connor Dotson found DeAree Rogers on a 24-yard touchdown pass, making it 14-7.

UMass answered before the half. Justin Williams-Thomas ran in a 19-yard touchdown with 1:01 left, and Derek Morris's extra point tied it at 14. That would have been the moment to carry some momentum into the break. Instead, NIU got the ball back and kicked the 45-yard field goal as the half expired, taking a 17-14 lead into the locker room.

The second half belonged to the defenses. Short added a 40-yard field goal with 5:26 left in the third quarter to make it 20-14, and nobody scored after that. UMass went the entire second half without a point.

## The run game worked. The rest didn't follow.

If there was a reason to be encouraged, it was in the backfield. Williams-Thomas carried 27 times for 138 yards and a touchdown, a 5.1-yard average, with a long of 24. The Minutemen as a team ran for 171 net yards on 40 carries, which was more than NIU managed on the ground (160 on 31 carries), and they held the ball for 32:26 to NIU's 27:34. They also had more first downs, 15 to 12, and ran 71 plays to NIU's 59. NIU did finish ahead in total yardage, 471 to 349, though both figures include punt and kick return yards.

But the passing game never gave the run game anything to work with. William Watson III was 14 of 31 for 135 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, and he ran five times for just 8 yards. His longest throw was a 44-yarder to tight end Matthew Ogunniyi, who finished with two catches for 45. Reece Adkins caught four passes for 28. The two senior receivers who looked like the headliners in the preview, Joseph Griffin Jr. and T.Y. Harding, caught four passes for 29 yards between them.

The third-down numbers were the sharpest sign of the problem. UMass converted 3 of 16, the same mark it posted in Week 1 at Rutgers. The Minutemen were 2 of 5 on fourth down and 1 of 2 in the red zone, where NIU was 1 of 1. A team that ran 71 plays and held the ball for more than 32 minutes left too many of them short of the sticks.

## The defense kept it close

On the other side, the defense gave UMass a chance. Head coach Joe Harasymiak's team got two NIU turnovers: Isaiah Reed intercepted Dotson and returned it 12 yards, and the dropped punt turned into UMass's first touchdown. Timmy Hinspeter led the team with eight tackles, and TJ Magee had seven. William Depaepe had a sack and two tackles for loss.

The problem was the ground. NIU's Telly Johnson Jr. ran 18 times for 157 yards, an average of 8.7, with a long of 36. Dotson was 16 of 26 for 183 yards, with a touchdown and an interception, and Rogers had seven catches for 91 yards and the score.

## What Cascieri said

"We did a lot of things right today. We won the turnover battle, we ran the ball, we had it longer than they did," Cascieri said. "And we still lost, because we were 3 of 16 on third down for the second week in a row and we didn't score in the second half. That's on me and it's on all of us. You can't give a team a field goal at the end of the half and then go quiet."

## The bigger picture

At 0-2, the arithmetic has changed. UMass now needs six wins from its final 10 games, and NIU was one of the nine opponents in the range where the season was supposed to be won. The home games against Miami (OH), Ball State and Akron are still ahead, and so is a trip to Sac State. But the margin for error is thin now, and the offense has not yet produced a game where the pass game and the run game worked together.

**Next up:** UMass hits the road for the Boston College rivalry game on Saturday, Sept. 19, a matchup that carries extra weight for Cascieri, who played for the Eagles.

title: UMass falls to in-state rival Boston College
dek: CHESTNUT HILL, Mass. — Boston College's Mason McKenzie broke a 73-yard touchdown run with 10:19 left in the first quarter, and the rest of the afternoon was a matter of how much UMass could claw back from that start. The answer, on the scoreboard, was not much.
body:
**Boston College 24, Massachusetts 3** · Week 3 · Sept. 19

CHESTNUT HILL, Mass. — Boston College's Mason McKenzie broke a 73-yard touchdown run with 10:19 left in the first quarter, and the rest of the afternoon was a matter of how much UMass could claw back from that start. The answer, on the scoreboard, was not much. But the more interesting story is what happened after it.

BC led 14-0 when the first quarter ended, after McKenzie hit Landon Wright for a 10-yard touchdown with 25 seconds left. From there, the Minutemen's defense spent the next three quarters keeping a better team from running away. BC scored 10 more points the rest of the way, and UMass, which is now 0-3, never found the end zone.

It was a rivalry game, and it carried extra weight for Sal Cascieri, who played at Boston College before coaching. It was also a game against an opponent ranked 82nd, well ahead of UMass at 136th. On that scale, the result is not a surprise. What matters is what UMass can take from it.

## The defense found its footing

The first quarter was a problem. After that, it was not.

Defensive coordinator Jared Keyte's unit gave up the 73-yard run and the short touchdown pass to Wright, then held BC to a third-quarter touchdown (a 5-yard pass from McKenzie to Wright with 28 seconds left in the period) and a fourth-quarter 35-yard field goal. McKenzie finished 15 of 27 for 176 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. BC ran for 151 yards on 35 carries, with Evan Dickens getting 82 yards on 24 of them.

Individually, Kendric Council was the best player on the field for UMass, with 11 tackles and three pass breakups. The pass rush found a way in, too. Andrew Depaepe, Zakar Morris and Tyler Martin each had a sack, for three total against one for BC's defense. Morris added two tackles for loss, and Isaiah Reed and Chris Stanley each forced a fumble, though Boston College held on to both and finished the game without a turnover.

That is a respectable response to a bad opening quarter.

## The offense never found its way in

The offense, by contrast, never really started.

UMass was 2 of 18 on third down, which is the headline number. It was 3 of 16 in each of the first two games, so the problem is a consistent one. The Minutemen never reached the red zone, finishing 0 of 0, and their only points came on a field goal from beyond 50 yards by Derek Morris with 6:22 left in the second quarter that cut the lead to 14-3.

There were some positives to find in the shape of the afternoon. UMass did not turn the ball over, after giving it away three times in Week 1 and once in Week 2. The Minutemen had more first downs (13 to 11), ran more plays (72 to 62), and held the ball for 30:10 to BC's 29:50. Boston College did finish ahead in total yardage, 359 to 264, though both figures include punt and kick return yards. They also went for it on fourth down five times and converted twice. The disadvantage was in what they did with all that: 72 plays produced 94 net passing yards and 108 rushing yards.

William Watson III was 13 of 36 for 94 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions, and he ran 10 times for 41 yards. T.Y. Harding led the receivers with three catches for 33 yards, Justin Williams-Thomas had two for 27 and rushed 14 times for 41 yards, a 2.9-yard average, and Joseph Griffin Jr. had one catch for 16 yards. Kezion Dia-Johnson caught three passes for minus-3 yards.

Penalties did not help. UMass was flagged six times for 57 yards against one for 10 for Boston College.

## The injury picture

Starting left guard Aitor Urionabarrenechea, who has a quad tear, is out eight weeks, and Melvin is out four. UMass also had a long list of players sit out practice because of injury risk, a group that included Watson, Griffin, Williams-Thomas and tight end Reece Adkins along with center Peyton Miller, tackles Greg Knox and Zachary Franks and guard Brock Taylor.

## What Cascieri said

"Obviously this one was personal for me, and I'm not going to pretend it wasn't. But that's not why we lost," Cascieri said. "We played a better team. I thought our defense settled in after the first quarter, we didn't turn it over, and Derek made a long kick. Those things are good. But 2 for 18 on third down doesn't beat anybody, and we never got inside the 20. We have to find a way to move the ball."

## The bigger picture

At 0-3, the bowl math is getting tight. UMass needs six wins and has nine games left, which means it must go 6-3 the rest of the way. Eight of the nine opponents left are ranked close to UMass, with Eastern Michigan the exception, so the schedule does soften from here. But the offense has to find some way to convert third downs and finish drives, because three points is not going to win many of those games.

**Next up:** UMass opens MAC play on the road at Sac State on Saturday, Sept. 26.

title: UMass falls to FBS newbie Sac Sate
dek: SACRAMENTO, Calif. — The schedule had marked this one in a particular way. Sac State was the only team on the Minutemen's slate ranked below them, 138th to UMass's 136th, a program new to the FBS and the one opponent where the rankings favored UMass.
body:
**Sac State 23, Massachusetts 10** · Week 4 · Sept. 26

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — The schedule had marked this one in a particular way. Sac State was the only team on the Minutemen's slate ranked below them, 138th to UMass's 136th, a program new to the FBS and the one opponent where the rankings favored UMass. It was also the first conference game of the season, and a chance to get a first win after an 0-3 start.

For 50 minutes, it was a game UMass could have won. Derek Morris's 42-yard field goal with 9:49 left in the fourth quarter cut it to 13-10. Then Jamar Curtis found a hole, Sac State scored the next 10 points, and the Minutemen were left with their fourth loss in four tries.

## Curtis was the difference

Sac State won this game on the ground, and mostly with one player. Curtis carried 25 times for 222 yards, an average of 8.9, with a long of 41 and a touchdown, and Sac State ran for 248 net yards on 39 carries. That is 6.4 yards per attempt, and it explains how a team that was nearly even with UMass in first downs and time of possession ended up with a 13-point win.

The score to make it 20-10 came with 7:16 left, from Curtis, 2:33 after UMass had pulled within a field goal. Grant Meadors added a field goal with 5:18 to play, and that was all the margin Sac State needed. Meadors made three of his five field goal attempts, so it could have been closer.

The Minutemen's defense, run by coordinator Jared Keyte, had some individual moments. Kendric Council led the team with 10 tackles and two tackles for loss, Timmy Hinspeter had nine, and TJ Magee had seven. Sac State's quarterback, Carson Conklin, was held to 13 of 25 for 139 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions, and Sac State never scored on a pass. But when the game was there to be won late, the run defense could not make a stop.

## An offense that never stretched the field

The reason it all mattered is that UMass could not score enough to make a defensive stand matter.

William Watson III was 17 of 32 for 90 yards, with a touchdown and no interceptions. His longest completion was 13 yards, and the team's longest run was 16, his own. UMass's longest play from scrimmage was 16 yards. Joseph Griffin Jr. caught four passes for 23 yards and the touchdown that tied the game at 7-7 with 6:57 left in the second quarter. T.Y. Harding had two catches for 14 yards. Reece Adkins caught four passes for six yards, and Justin Williams-Thomas caught four for 25.

The pass protection was part of the problem. Sac State sacked Watson five times, with Fata Puloka getting two of them, and UMass's offensive line is playing without starting left guard Aitor Urionabarrenechea, who is out eight weeks. Watson also carried the ball 13 times for 44 yards, a 3.4-yard average, and Williams-Thomas ran 15 times for 72 yards.

There were some better numbers underneath. UMass was 6 of 16 on third down, a real improvement after 3 of 16, 3 of 16 and 2 of 18 in the first three games. The Minutemen had 17 first downs to Sac State's 16, committed just one penalty for 10 yards, and were 1 of 1 in the red zone. Morris was 1 of 2 on field goals. Sac State finished with 425 total yards to UMass's 310, though both figures include punt and kick return yards.

UMass's one turnover was a fumble that Sac State recovered.

## What Cascieri said

"I'm not going to dress it up. We had a chance in the fourth quarter, we were down three, and we didn't make a play," Cascieri said. "Ninety yards through the air isn't going to win a game in this league. That's a game we should have won, and that's on me. We have to find a way to throw the ball and protect the quarterback."

## The bigger picture

At 0-4, UMass needs six wins from its remaining eight games to reach a bowl, which means going 6-2 the rest of the way. The path is still open on paper, with four of those eight games at home, but it leaves almost no room for another slip.

**Next up:** UMass returns home for a Saturday, Oct. 3 meeting with Eastern Michigan, the top team in the MAC's preseason order.

title: UMass snaps 19 game losing streak with win against Eastern Michigan
dek: AMHERST, Mass. — The Minutemen ran 93 plays. They held the ball for 41 minutes and 27 seconds. They had 27 first downs to Eastern Michigan's 12. And with 11:29 left in the fourth quarter, they trailed 17-10.
body:
**Massachusetts 20, Eastern Michigan 17** · Week 5 · Oct. 3

AMHERST, Mass. — The Minutemen ran 93 plays. They held the ball for 41 minutes and 27 seconds. They had 27 first downs to Eastern Michigan's 12. And with 11:29 left in the fourth quarter, they trailed 17-10.

That is the shape of the afternoon, and it is why the first win of UMass's season arrived the way it did, with 10 unanswered points over the final minutes. Derek Morris kicked a 26-yard field goal with 2:45 left to make it 17-13, and with 37 seconds to play, William Watson III threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Ogunniyi. Morris's extra point made it 20-17, and after four losses to start the year, UMass had something to celebrate.

It also came against the highest-ranked opponent the Minutemen have faced in conference play. Eastern Michigan was 71st in the media rankings to UMass's 136th, and it came into the day first in the MAC's preseason order.

## A defense that took the game away

The defense is what kept this game within reach long enough to win. Head coach Joe Harasymiak's team, with Jared Keyte coordinating the defense, held Eastern Michigan to five net rushing yards on 19 carries. Braydon Bennett ran 13 times for 22 yards, and quarterback Noah Kim lost 19 yards on five carries. Eastern Michigan had 12 first downs and converted 4 of 13 third downs, and it held the ball for just 18:33.

Samuel Mulbah and William Depaepe each sacked Kim, and Kendric Council led the team with seven tackles, a tackle for loss and a pass breakup. TJ Magee had six tackles, and Isaiah Reed and Zeraun Daniel had five apiece. The one area that gave Eastern Michigan life was the passing game. Kim was 18 of 34 for 226 yards and two touchdowns, including 80 yards on four catches by Benson Prosper, who scored the 11-yard touchdown that put Eastern Michigan ahead 17-10.

## An offense that moved the ball, and finished some of the time

The offense had its best day of the season by almost every measure, even if the finish on some of those drives was less than ideal.

UMass had 501 total yards to Eastern Michigan's 254, though both figures include punt and kick return yards. The Minutemen ran for 231 yards on 47 carries and threw for 223. They did it with a committee: Elijah Faulkner had 15 carries for 55 yards, Jordan Washington 11 for 53, Watson 9 for 50, Trace Pullen four for 43, including a 37-yard run, and Justin Williams-Thomas eight for 30.

Watson was 27 of 46 for 223 yards with two touchdowns and one interception, and he picked up 50 yards on the ground. Reece Adkins was his favorite target, catching eight passes for 78 yards and a 5-yard touchdown in the second quarter. T.Y. Harding had seven catches for 52 yards, and Ogunniyi caught two passes for 22 yards, including the winner.

The Minutemen converted 9 of 22 third downs and went for it on fourth down eight times, converting five of them. UMass punted only twice all day. They also did it without starting left guard Aitor Urionabarrenechea, who is out eight weeks.

The flip side is the thing that kept the game in doubt. UMass reached the red zone eight times and scored on four of them. They turned it over once, on a Watson interception by Donmiel Rogers, and Eastern Michigan's punter averaged 47.0 yards on seven punts, two of them inside the 20. A team that dominated possession, plays and first downs to this degree would normally have been ahead by more than it was.

## What Cascieri said

"The defense won us this game, and I want to say that first. Five rushing yards on 19 carries, that's remarkable," Cascieri said. "Offensively, I'm proud of how we fought, and we converted fourth downs when we needed to. But we were 4 of 8 in the red zone, and we have to finish. We left points on the field and made it harder than it needed to be."

## The bigger picture

At 1-4, UMass needs five more wins from its final seven games to get to six, which is the bowl threshold. All seven of the opponents left are ranked between 113th and 132nd, in the same range as UMass, which keeps the path open on paper. The Minutemen can't afford many slow starts or lost chances from here, but the way UMass controlled the ball against the top team in the league's preseason order is something to build on.

**Next up:** UMass stays home to face Miami (OH) on Saturday, Oct. 10.

title: Undefeated no more: UMass pulls off upset.
dek: AMHERST, Mass. — Miami (OH) arrived undefeated and left having scored on exactly one drive. That drive came early, with 5:00 left in the first quarter on a 1-yard touchdown run by Cade Yacamelli, and it was the last time Miami would reach the end zone.
body:
**Massachusetts 16, Miami (OH) 7** · Week 6 · Oct. 10

AMHERST, Mass. — Miami (OH) arrived undefeated and left having scored on exactly one drive. That drive came early, with 5:00 left in the first quarter on a 1-yard touchdown run by Cade Yacamelli, and it was the last time Miami would reach the end zone. UMass shut them out the rest of the way, and the Minutemen's offense did just enough to turn a quiet afternoon into back-to-back wins.

It is a result that changes the shape of UMass's season. A team that started 0-4 is now 2-4, and a team that was staring at long odds for a bowl game has two straight conference wins, one of them over an unbeaten opponent.

## A defense that kept getting the ball back

The defense was the story again. Head coach Joe Harasymiak's team, with Jared Keyte coordinating, held Miami to 96 rushing yards, 188 passing and seven points. Miami's David McComb was 14 of 27 for 188 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, both by TJ Magee, who returned them for 39 yards combined. McComb also lost nine yards on seven carries.

Miami had one productive runner in Rodney Nelson, who carried 20 times for 104 yards with a long of 35, and one productive receiver in Keith Reynolds, who caught five passes for 106 yards. Beyond that, UMass held the Miami offense to 3 of 11 on third downs and just 14 first downs. Zakar Morris had a sack, Kendall Bournes and Andrew Depaepe shared one, and Timmy Hinspeter led the team with eight tackles. Isaiah Reed had seven, and Kendric Council had six.

The Minutemen also won the field position game in a quiet way. Edward Phillipson punted four times for a 34.3-yard average, and all four landed inside the 20-yard line. Miami's Pierse Stainton punted six times for a 50.0-yard average, and none of them were downed inside the 20.

## An offense that finished, mostly

After the red zone problems that cost UMass in the Eastern Michigan game, the offense showed more discipline against Miami. The Minutemen were 3 of 3 in the red zone, a clear step up from 4 of 8 against Eastern Michigan, and 9 of 18 on third down. They had 18 first downs to Miami's 14, ran 69 plays to 55, and held the ball for 38:42 to Miami's 21:18. Total yardage was 351 to 324 in UMass's favor, with both figures including punt and kick return yards.

The scoring was efficient, if not spectacular. Derek Morris was 3 for 3 on field goals with a long of 47, and UMass scored its lone touchdown on a Watson pass to Reece Adkins with 1:25 left in the second quarter. That gave the Minutemen a 10-7 lead at the half, after a Morris field goal with 11:03 left in the quarter had cut it to 7-3. He added field goals with 7:16 and 1:56 left in the fourth quarter to put the game away.

William Watson III was 22 of 34 for 178 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions, and he carried four times for 19 yards. T.Y. Harding led the receivers with six catches for 55 yards, and Adkins had four for 34 and the touchdown. Justin Williams-Thomas ran 15 times for 66 yards and caught three passes for 31, and Elijah Faulkner had 15 carries for 42. The Minutemen threw for 178 and ran for 129, and they did it without turning the ball over.

One caution: for all the improvement in the red zone, UMass scored one touchdown and three field goals on the day, so the ceiling is still limited by how often drives end in six points instead of three.

## What Cascieri said

"That's a complete game from our defense, two interceptions, and they gave us the ball back all afternoon," Cascieri said. "We were 3 for 3 in the red zone and 9 of 18 on third down, and that's what we've been asking for. I'd still like to turn a couple of those field goals into touchdowns. But we didn't turn it over, and Derek was perfect."

## The bigger picture

At 2-4, UMass needs four wins from its final six games to reach six, the bowl threshold. All six opponents left are ranked between 114th and 132nd, in the same range as UMass, and the Minutemen have shown they can compete with that group, with back-to-back wins and a defense that is giving up few points. The margin remains thin, but the path is no longer remote.

**Next up:** UMass hits the road for the Flagship Cup game at Buffalo on Saturday, Oct. 17.

title: UMass runs for 276 yards, then lets a halftime lead and the whole second half slip away at Buffalo
dek: BUFFALO, N.Y. — It was a game UMass led at the half and did not score in after it. That is the short version of the Flagship Cup loss, and it is a painful one, because for 30 minutes the Minutemen looked like the team that had won two straight and the offense looked like it had…
body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. — It was a game UMass led at the half and did not score in after it. That is the short version of the Flagship Cup loss, and it is a painful one, because for 30 minutes the Minutemen looked like the team that had won two straight and the offense looked like it had found something.

Justin Williams-Thomas ran for two touchdowns in the first half, one with 8:03 left in the first quarter and another with 10:29 left in the second, to give UMass a 14-7 lead. He finished with 169 yards on 19 carries, an average of 8.9, with a long of 77. The Minutemen as a team ran for 276 yards on 38 attempts. By most measures, the ground game was the best it has been all year.

And then came the end of the half. UMass's only trip inside the Buffalo 20 ended with a William Watson III pass in the end zone that was intercepted by Zach Bergmann, taking away a chance to go into the break with a larger lead. The Minutemen did not score again.

## The second half got away

After a scoreless third quarter, Buffalo started to move the ball. Oliver Hautanen kicked a 35-yard field goal with 11:26 left in the fourth to make it 14-10, and with 7:09 to play, Elijah Holmes threw a touchdown pass to Jasaiah Gathings to give Buffalo a 17-14 lead. UMass had no answer.

The Buffalo offense kept the ball moving. It ran 78 plays to UMass's 62, had 19 first downs to 13, and Holmes was 21 of 35 for 207 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. Gathings caught seven passes for 78 yards and the go-ahead score, and Messiah Burch carried 29 times for 120 yards. Buffalo was flagged zero times, and UMass was flagged four times for 35 yards.

The defense, to its credit, was not the reason UMass lost. Head coach Joe Harasymiak's team, with Jared Keyte coordinating, held Buffalo to 17 points and recorded two sacks, from William Depaepe and Zakar Morris. Timmy Hinspeter led the way with 10 tackles, TJ Magee had eight and Chris Stanley seven. Aubrey Melvin also appeared on the stat sheet with three tackles, after missing time with an injury. But the offense never gave the defense much help in the second half.

## An offense that couldn't do both things

The ground game worked. The passing game did not, and the problem was not subtle.

Watson was 10 of 23 for 68 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, and his longest completion was 17 yards. T.Y. Harding had three catches for 22 yards, Reece Adkins had three for 19, and Williams-Thomas caught one pass for 16. Watson did contribute on the ground, with four carries for 46 yards and a long of 21, and Elijah Faulkner had 13 carries for 47.

UMass was 5 of 16 on third down, and Buffalo was 5 of 17, so neither side had much success there. The Minutemen were 1 of 2 on fourth down, and Derek Morris was 0 for 1 on field goals. Total yardage was nearly even, 402 for UMass and 407 for Buffalo, though both figures include punt and kick return yards. UMass held the ball for 30:42 to Buffalo's 29:18.

It is a long way to lose a game when you rush for 276 yards. The difference was a passing game that gave UMass 68 yards, one red-zone trip that ended in a turnover, and a second half with no points.

## What Cascieri said

"We gave this one away," Cascieri said. "We had the lead at the half, we had a chance to extend it, and the ball ends up in the wrong hands in the end zone. Then we didn't do anything in the second half. Justin ran great, 276 yards on the ground should win you a game. We can't be one-dimensional. That's on all of us, starting with me."

## The bigger picture

At 2-5, UMass would need to win four of its last five games to reach six wins. All five remaining opponents, UConn, Ball State, Toledo, Akron and Bowling Green, are ranked between 114th and 132nd, so the path is open on paper. But it no longer has any margin, and it will take an offense that can score in the second half.

**Next up:** UMass travels to UConn for the rivalry game on Saturday, Oct. 24.

title: UMass holds the ball for 46 minutes, gives Ball State four first downs and wins its most complete conference game of the year
dek: AMHERST, Mass. — The statistic that tells the story of this game is not the score. It is the clock. UMass held the ball for 46 minutes and 9 seconds, and Ball State held it for 13:51. The Minutemen ran 89 plays to Ball State's 38. They had 26 first downs, and Ball State had four.
body:
AMHERST, Mass. — The statistic that tells the story of this game is not the score. It is the clock. UMass held the ball for 46 minutes and 9 seconds, and Ball State held it for 13:51. The Minutemen ran 89 plays to Ball State's 38. They had 26 first downs, and Ball State had four.

That is not a game that was ever in much doubt, and the 22-7 final reflects it, but it is also a game that could have been far more lopsided. Ball State's one touchdown came on a long run by quarterback Keldric Luster, a score that tied the game 7-7 barely a minute after UMass had taken the lead. After that, Ball State never scored, never completed more than a handful of passes and never really threatened.

For a team that had been 0-4 and then 2-5, it was a convincing step: the Minutemen are now 4-5, 3-2 in the MAC, and have won four of their last five.

## A defense that was barely on the field

The numbers on the defensive side are strange to read because there were so few of them. Head coach Joe Harasymiak's team, with Jared Keyte coordinating the defense, held Ball State to four first downs, 38 net passing yards and 1-of-10 on third down. Luster was 5 of 17 for 38 yards and carried six times for 69 yards, a total built on a touchdown run of more than 70 yards. TJ Horton had 14 carries for 52. Ball State also went 0 for 2 on fourth down.

Andrew Depaepe had a sack and two tackles for loss, and Kendall Bournes and Kendric Council had five tackles apiece. Aubrey Melvin, back after missing time, had four. Ball State rarely had the ball long enough to do anything with it.

## An offense that moved the ball, and settled for too many field goals

The Minutemen's 89 plays produced 215 rushing yards on 49 carries and 168 passing yards. They had 496 total yards to Ball State's 289, with both figures including punt and kick return yards. They did it without a turnover and with a perfect day from the kicker. Derek Morris made all three of his field goals, from 24, 41 and 35 yards.

The part of the box score UMass would like to change is how many of those drives ended in three points. The Minutemen were 4 of 6 in the red zone, and they scored two touchdowns and three field goals on the day. They were also 3 of 16 on third down, a number that was bailed out by a 4-of-6 conversion rate on fourth down. A team that gets that many snaps and that much of the ball should have more than 22 points.

Justin Williams-Thomas scored the first touchdown, from two yards out with 7:52 left in the second quarter, and finished with 94 yards on 19 carries. Elijah Faulkner had 16 carries for 90 yards, a 5.6-yard average, and Jordan Washington added 22. William Watson III was 22 of 40 for 168 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. His one touchdown pass was a 1-yarder to Kezion Dia-Johnson with 2:24 left, though the conversion try failed. T.Y. Harding led the receivers with six catches for 43 yards, Reece Adkins had four for 40, and Joseph Griffin Jr. had four for 36.

## What Cascieri said

"I'm really proud of how we played. We had the ball for 46 minutes and their offense barely saw the field," Cascieri said. "But I'll be honest about the other side of it: 22 points on 89 plays isn't good enough. We were 4 for 6 in the red zone and 3 for 16 on third down. We have to finish drives. The fourth-down conversions bailed us out, and we're not going to get away with that every week."

## The bigger picture

At 4-5, UMass needs two wins from its last three games to reach six, the bowl threshold. The remaining games are at Toledo, home against Akron and at Bowling Green. The Minutemen have won four of their last five, but the next test is a much harder one.

**Next up:** UMass travels to Toledo on Wednesday, Nov. 11, to face 7-1 Toledo in a primetime ESPN game before a gold-out crowd.

title: UMass wins without a touchdown: three Morris field goals, 14-of-23 on third down and a defense that allows one score
dek: AMHERST, Mass. — The final score is the kind that gets written in the margins of a program's season. UMass beat Akron 9-7 without scoring a touchdown, on three field goals from Derek Morris, in a game where the Minutemen ran 81 plays, held the ball for 38 minutes and 16 seconds…
body:
AMHERST, Mass. — The final score is the kind that gets written in the margins of a program's season. UMass beat Akron 9-7 without scoring a touchdown, on three field goals from Derek Morris, in a game where the Minutemen ran 81 plays, held the ball for 38 minutes and 16 seconds and picked up 22 first downs.

It was the first win of the year for UMass without a touchdown, and it moved the Minutemen to 5-6 and 4-3 in the MAC. It was also a win that came uncomfortably close to going the other way, because of the one thing the offense could not do all night: get into the end zone.

## The same story as the box score

The scoring summary is short. Morris made a 34-yard field goal with 6:49 left in the second quarter to give UMass a 3-0 lead. Akron answered on a 1-yard touchdown run by quarterback Reese Poffenbarger with 4:51 left in the half, and Akron led 7-3. Morris kicked a 30-yarder as time expired in the half to make it 7-6, and he added a 19-yarder with 11:57 left in the fourth quarter to put UMass ahead 9-7. Nobody scored again.

The Minutemen were 3 of 3 in the red zone, but all three trips ended in field goals. The rest of the numbers say the offense should have scored more. UMass converted 14 of 23 third downs, a leap from the 3-of-16 marks it posted four times earlier this season, and it outgained Akron 405 yards to 329, though both figures include punt and kick return yards. It had 22 first downs to Akron's 16.

The ground game did most of the work. The Minutemen ran for 209 yards on 42 carries, and Akron ran for 63. William Watson III had his best game as a runner, carrying nine times for 103 yards, an average of 11.4, with a long of 37. Elijah Faulkner had 19 carries for 66 yards, Justin Williams-Thomas had 10 for 24, and Jordan Washington had four for 16.

Watson was 18 of 39 for 165 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, and Akron's Dawayne Galloway Jr. returned it 28 yards. Joseph Griffin Jr. led the receivers with four catches for 55 yards, Kezion Dia-Johnson had three for 50, and Reece Adkins had three for 25. The Minutemen also punted five times, with Edward Phillipson putting three of them inside the 20.

## A defense that gave up one score

The defense was the reason the game was close enough for field goals to matter. Head coach Joe Harasymiak's team, with Jared Keyte coordinating the defense, held Akron to 63 net rushing yards, 5 of 13 on third down and seven points. Poffenbarger was 17 of 34 for 201 yards with no touchdown passes and one interception, by DD Snyder, and he lost 14 yards on eight carries. Jordan Gant led Akron on the ground with 18 carries for 74 yards.

Kendric Council had 10 tackles and two pass breakups. Tyler Martin had nine tackles, two tackles for loss and a sack, Chris Stanley had nine, and Andrew Depaepe had five with a sack and a tackle for loss. Akron had the ball for just 21:44.

## What Cascieri said

"A win is a win, and I'm not going to apologize for it," Cascieri said. "Derek won us that game, and our defense gave up seven points, which is outstanding. But we were 3 for 3 in the red zone and we kicked three field goals. We moved the ball all night and we have to score touchdowns. That's the thing we've been talking about for weeks, and we have to fix it."

## The bigger picture

At 5-6, UMass needs one more win to reach six, the bowl threshold, and it will have one chance left. The Minutemen have won five of their last eight, and they now go on the road for a regular-season finale where a win would make them bowl-eligible.

**Next up:** UMass closes the regular season on the road at Bowling Green on Saturday, Nov. 28.

title: UMass falls one win short of a bowl bid in the rain at Bowling Green, undone by Austyn Dendy and three turnovers of its own
dek: BOWLING GREEN, Ohio — The season came down to one game, and in heavy rain, it did not go UMass's way. The Minutemen needed a win at Bowling Green to reach six wins and become bowl-eligible.
body:
BOWLING GREEN, Ohio — The season came down to one game, and in heavy rain, it did not go UMass's way. The Minutemen needed a win at Bowling Green to reach six wins and become bowl-eligible. They took the ball away three times, ran 74 plays to Bowling Green's 54, held it for 34:35, and still walked off the field a 27-14 loser.

The final record is 5-7, 4-4 in the MAC. It is a season that started 0-4 and then turned into something respectable, and it ends one win short of the postseason.

## The game that got away

The way UMass lost this one is a long list of small things, and the biggest of them has a name: Austyn Dendy. The Bowling Green running back carried 19 times for 185 yards, an average of 9.7, and scored three touchdowns, from 3 yards out in the second quarter, 43 yards with 8:24 left in the third and 39 yards with 8:29 left in the fourth. Bowling Green ran for 215 yards as a team, and those three scores accounted for most of their offense. Kicker Ethan Warner added field goals of 45 and 49 yards.

UMass led 3-0 after Derek Morris kicked a field goal in the first quarter, and trailed 10-3 at the half. After Morris made a 41-yarder with 10:03 left in the third quarter, Dendy broke the 43-yard run to make it 17-6, and UMass answered with a 1-yard touchdown pass from William Watson III to Matthew Ogunniyi, followed by a good two-point conversion, to cut it to 17-14 with 3:47 left in the quarter. Then came the fourth quarter. Dendy scored again to make it 24-14, and Warner's 49-yard field goal with 5:02 left made it 27-14.

## Turnovers, kicks and a call

The Minutemen did a lot right and more wrong in the margins. They forced three turnovers: Kendall Bournes intercepted Jay Kastantin, and Kendric Council forced a fumble, recovered two and made seven tackles. But UMass also gave the ball away three times, on a Watson interception and two lost fumbles.

Morris was 2 for 5 on field goals, with a long of 42, in the rain. Three missed kicks in a game that ended with a 13-point margin is the kind of thing that matters. UMass was also sacked four times, with Myles Bradley getting two of them.

Then there was the last fumble. With about four minutes left, with UMass inside the red zone and trailing 27-14, the quarterback's arm appeared to the UMass sideline to be moving forward when the ball came out, and the play was ruled a fumble instead of an incompletion. Bowling Green took over, and the drive ended without points. UMass was 2 of 3 in the red zone on the day. At that point, the Minutemen were still down 13, so the call did not by itself decide the game, but it ended UMass's best chance to make the finish interesting.

## The offense moved it again

The offense did produce. UMass had 451 total yards to Bowling Green's 416, though both figures include punt and kick return yards, and 19 first downs to 12. The Minutemen were 7 of 18 on third down and 2 of 2 on fourth down.

Justin Williams-Thomas ran 19 times for 99 yards, with a long of 30, and Watson had 10 carries for 56. Watson was 21 of 37 for 190 yards with one touchdown and one interception. T.Y. Harding caught six passes for 64 yards, Reece Adkins had four for 48, and Kezion Dia-Johnson had two for 28.

William Depaepe had two sacks and three tackles for loss for a defense that, under coordinator Jared Keyte and head coach Joe Harasymiak, sacked Kastantin twice and held Bowling Green's passing game to 123 yards. Kastantin was 11 of 20 with one interception.

## What Cascieri said

"That's a tough one. We needed it, and we had chances," Cascieri said. "We took the ball away three times and didn't turn that into enough points. We were 2 for 5 on field goals in the rain, and we put the ball on the ground when we had it. I thought the quarterback's arm was going forward on that last one, and I'll leave it at that. But we had other chances before that. I'm proud of how this group fought. We started 0-4 and we won five games, and that's something to build on."

## The bigger picture

UMass finishes 5-7. That is one win short of bowl eligibility, but it is also more wins than the program had ever recorded in a season at the FBS level before this year. The Minutemen won five of their last nine games after the 0-4 start, with wins over Eastern Michigan, Miami (OH), UConn, Ball State and Akron, and a 4-4 MAC record.

**Next up:** The regular season is over. UMass finishes at 5-7 and misses a bowl bid by one win.
